subject: English
central_question: When professional duty, human compassion and national loyalty conflict during war, what choices allow Dr Sadao and Hana to preserve life without ignoring danger?
in_scope_units: Before you Read: the wartime dilemma of a Japanese doctor finding an American prisoner.
Dr Sadao’s coastal home, his father’s influence, medical education in America and marriage to Hana.
The wounded American sailor on the beach and the decision to carry him inside.
The servants’ resistance, Hana’s assistance and Sadao’s operation.
The prisoner’s recovery, the servants’ departure and Sadao’s unresolved report to the police.
Sadao’s disclosure to the General and the promised private assassination.
The General’s failure to act, Sadao’s escape plan and the prisoner’s departure by boat.
The General’s self-absorbed explanation and Sadao’s final question about why he could not kill the man.
Reading with Insight Questions 1–8 on hard choices, Hana, the soldier, the General, prejudice and the final solution.
banned_topics: A general history of the Second World War beyond the wartime setting in the story.
Legal rules for prisoners of war not stated in the chapter.
Medical instructions for surgery or anaesthesia beyond the narrated operation.

known_pitfalls.claim: Sadao saves the prisoner because he supports America.
known_pitfalls.correction: He repeatedly calls Americans enemies; he acts because his training and humanity will not let a wounded man die.

known_pitfalls.claim: Hana immediately accepts the prisoner without fear or prejudice.
known_pitfalls.correction: She feels fear and repulsion, yet washes, assists and feeds him because he is wounded and helpless.

known_pitfalls.claim: The General forgets the assassination plan out of mercy.
known_pitfalls.correction: He admits that he thought only of himself while ill and forgot his promise.

known_pitfalls.claim: Sadao hands Tom directly to the police after recovery.
known_pitfalls.correction: He eventually supplies a boat, food, clothing and directions so Tom can escape.

recommended_example_progression: Use Reading with Insight Q1 to establish the conflict between private humanity and national loyalty.
Use Reading with Insight Q2 to analyse Hana’s sympathy despite the servants’ defiance.
Use Reading with Insight Q4 to examine the General’s self-absorption.
Use Reading with Insight Q6 to evaluate Sadao’s escape plan.
Use Reading with Insight Q5 to interpret the final movement beyond racial prejudice.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter concludes with Reading with Insight Questions 1–8 on role conflict, Hana, the soldier, the General, prejudice, Sadao’s solution and thematic comparisons.
